purpose: Rizatriptan is used to treat migraine headaches once they have started. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with migraines. It is not used to prevent migraines from happening in the first place.
how_it_works: When a migraine starts, certain blood vessels in your brain swell up and cause pain. Rizatriptan works by narrowing those blood vessels back to their normal size. It also blocks pain signals from being sent to your brain, which helps the headache go away faster.
common_side_effects: You may feel dizzy, drowsy, or tired after taking it. Some people feel a warm, tingling, or pressure sensation in the chest, neck, or throat — this is usually harmless but let your doctor know if it happens. Nausea, dry mouth, and headache are also possible.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you have heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or a history of stroke. Avoid taking it within 24 hours of other triptans or ergotamine-type migraine medicines. If you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden severe headache after taking it, seek medical help right away. Tell your doctor about all your medications, especially antidepressants, as serious interactions can occur.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg or 10 mg taken by mouth at the first sign of a migraine. If the headache comes back after getting better, you can take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first one. Do not take more than 30 mg in one day. The dissolving tablet (MLT) can be placed on your tongue without water, which is handy if you feel nauseous.
